intro: In a basketball arena, 70% of the fans are rooting for the home team. 25% of the fans are wearing blue. 20% of the fans are wearing blue and are rooting for the away team. Of the fans rooting for the away team, 67% are wearing blue. Let A be the event that a fan is rooting for the away team. Let B be the event that a fan is wearing blue.
question: Are the events of rooting for the away team and wearing blue independent?
answer: No. P(B) = 0.25, but P(B | A) = 0.67. Independent events would have P(B | A) = P(B).
hint: P(A) = 1 − 0.70. To test independence, compare P(B | A) with P(B).

intro: The scores on a college entrance exam have an approximate normal distribution with mean μ = 52 points and standard deviation σ = 11 points.

intro: The proportion of students who view class lecture videos is 55%. We randomly take a sample of 60 students.
question: What are the mean and standard deviation of the distribution of sample proportions?
answer: Mean = 0.55. Standard deviation = √(0.55 × 0.45 / 60) ≈ 0.0642. The normal model applies because np = 33 and nq = 27 are both at least 10.
hint: For a sample proportion, the standard deviation is √(p(1 − p) / n). Check that np and nq are both at least 10 before you use the normal model.

intro: The proportion of students who view class lecture videos is 55%. We randomly take a sample of 60 students.

answer: Reading “10% away” as 10 percentage points, that means p̂ < 0.45 or p̂ > 0.65. z = ±0.10 / 0.0642 ≈ ±1.56, so the probability is about 0.1195.
hint: For a sample proportion, the standard deviation is √(p(1 − p) / n). Check that np and nq are both at least 10 before you use the normal model.
